sections.model_projection: The model projects Chicago Bears 23.26, Carolina Panthers 21.93, for a projected total of 45.18 with the Bears favored by 1.33 points. The Bears' win probability is 57.01% (Panthers 41.99%). The market currently has Carolina as a 3-point home favorite, meaning the model leans 1.67 points toward the Bears relative to the market line, and sits 1.32 points under the market total of 46.5.
sections.offensive_matchup: Chicago's offense grades out significantly better than Carolina's, ranking 7th in EPA per play (a measure of how many expected points each play generates, positive is good) at +0.085 versus Carolina's 26th-ranked mark of -0.084. The Bears also convert at a 46.3% offensive success rate (rank 10th) while the Panthers manage just 41.5% (rank 25th). Carolina's defense allows a 46.2% opponent success rate (rank 21st), which means Chicago's offense should find consistent down-to-down traction. Carolina's offense, meanwhile, faces a Bears defense that sits at a middling 18th in defensive EPA per play at +0.030, so the Panthers can move the ball but are unlikely to sustain drives at a high rate.
sections.quarterback_edge: Caleb Williams carries a career EPA per dropback of 0.00 across 1,229 attempts and 36 games, while Bryce Young sits at -0.145 over 1,431 attempts and 45 games — a meaningful gap in efficiency. Williams also averages 6.6 yards per attempt versus Young's 5.98. Young has thrown 31 interceptions against 50 touchdowns in his career, a TD-to-INT ratio that reflects the negative EPA mark. The QB edge is one of the two largest point contributors favoring Chicago in the model, worth roughly 0.77 points toward the Bears.
sections.trenches: The trench battle cuts in opposite directions. Carolina's offensive line grades favorably in the OFFENSIVE_LINE edge (score +2 for home), contributing 0.64 points toward the Panthers, driven by a run-blocking-versus-run-defense composite that strongly favors Carolina's blockers against Chicago's run defense, which ranks 24th in rushing EPA allowed. However, Chicago's defensive front dominates the DEFENSIVE_FRONT edge at -3 (favoring away), worth 0.81 points toward the Bears — the single largest edge in the model. Chicago's pass rush faces a Panthers offensive line that allows pressure on 24.3% of dropbacks (rank 25th), while Carolina's pass rush generates pressure on only 17.7% of dropbacks without the blitz (rank 30th), making it difficult to rattle Williams.
sections.explosive_play_edge: Chicago generates explosive plays (10+ yards rushing or 20+ passing) on 9.8% of plays (rank 9th), while Carolina produces them on just 7.9% (rank 22nd). The Bears' advantage is partially offset by their own defense allowing explosives at a 10.5% rate (rank 28th), one of the worst marks in the league, while Carolina's defense limits explosives to just 7.8% (rank 9th). The net edge favors Chicago slightly, contributing 0.10 points toward the Bears, but Carolina's defense is genuinely capable of suppressing big plays even if it struggles in other areas.
sections.third_down_red_zone: Chicago converts third downs at a 43.6% rate (rank 6th) against a Panthers defense that allows conversions on 46.2% of third downs (rank 30th) — a stark mismatch that gives the Bears a strong path to sustained drives. Carolina converts just 36.7% of its own third downs (rank 25th), and the Bears' defense holds opponents to a 40.5% conversion rate (rank 16th), compounding the Panthers' difficulty. In the red zone, Chicago scores touchdowns on 63.4% of trips (rank 13th) while Carolina's defense allows TDs on 54.3% of red-zone visits (rank 8th, a genuine strength). Carolina's offense scores touchdowns on only 54.2% of red-zone trips (rank 23rd), and earns just 2.39 points per scoring opportunity (rank 28th), making field goals a likely outcome when they do reach scoring range.
sections.roster_talent: Insufficient reliable data. Both teams show similar roster continuity indices (Chicago 0.85, Carolina 0.86) and neither has a talent rating available in the model. Chicago returns 76% of total production with full passing continuity (100%) and strong rushing continuity (96%), while Carolina returns 77% overall with 93% passing and 84% receiving continuity but only 48% rushing continuity. Carolina's offensive line logs 57 returning starts versus Chicago's 68, a gap that may reflect the Bears' stronger pass-protection metrics.
sections.recent_form: Both teams are entering Week 1 with zero games played in the 2026 season, so no in-season form data is available. The model's RECENT_FORM edge is neutral with a 0.0 shift for both teams. All metrics carry a low-sample flag and are derived from prior-season blended data.

The total has held steady at 47.5 with no movement. Book disagreement on the spread is 0.5 points across the nine books sampled. sections.expected_game_script: Chicago's fast-paced offense — averaging 66.1 plays per game (rank 1st) at 29.8 seconds per play (rank 4th) — should control tempo from the opening drive, putting pressure on a Carolina defense that generates pressure on only 17.7% of dropbacks without the blitz (rank 30th). Williams, operating behind an offensive line that allows sacks on just 3.4% of dropbacks (rank 1st), should have time to work through progressions and exploit Carolina's 30th-ranked third-down defense. Carolina's offense will lean on its run game, where the Panthers' offensive line grades favorably against Chicago's 31st-ranked line-yards-allowed defense, but Bryce Young's passing struggles will make it difficult to sustain drives when the ground game stalls. The Bears' 32.1% play-action rate (rank 2nd) against a Panthers defense that generates pressure without the blitz on only 8.7% of dropbacks (rank 30th) sets up a significant schematic advantage for Chicago's passing attack. Carolina's best path to staying competitive is limiting explosive plays — where their defense ranks 9th — and capitalizing on Chicago's porous red-zone defense, which allows touchdowns on 67.3% of opponent trips. Expect a moderate-scoring game that trends below the 46.5 market total, with Chicago building a lead through third-down efficiency and turnover margin while Carolina struggles to convert scoring opportunities into touchdowns. The Bears' edge in nearly every efficiency category points to a close but Chicago-controlled outcome, with the Panthers' home field and run-blocking advantage keeping the margin within single digits.
